topIssues.title: op-conductor: support reorgs
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
Conductor currently *never* expects a chain regression from the Sequencers.

This means that if there is ever a protocol-caused regression of the chain, the Conductor will deem all sequencers unhealthy, causing a chain stall.

We need to upgrade conductor to follow reorgs. This is especially important for Interop, where experiencing and recovering from an invalid message is paramount.

topIssues.title: kona-interop: Review access of blocks created internally
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
Currently when Kona-proofs interop performs the interop validation step, if the first validation pass identifies blocks that need to be replaced, it builds them and sets them as chain head then does another validation pass to see if that has caused other chains to become invalid.  But in the second pass it loads the deposit-only block it just generated from the preimage oracle. This block will be canonical so the load will work, but given the block was just built this is a suspicious design choice.

If it ever asks the preimage oracle from a block that isn't canonical (eg an optimistic block it just derived which is later replaced), it would cause failures.  We should review for safety and consider prioritising first checking if the block is already known before loading from the oracle.

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: add real regression guard for EL restart SYNCING recovery
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Context

PR #19384 fixes a stall in `EngineController.tryUpdateEngineInternal`: when an EL returns `SYNCING` to a forkchoice update (e.g. after an op-reth restart that loses in-memory canonical state), op-node previously recorded the FCU as accepted and never retried. The fix triggers a pipeline reset in CL-sync mode so `FindL2Heads` can re-discover the EL's actual chain state.

The PR originally included an acceptance test at `op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/el_restart/TestELRestartRecovery` that exercised this flow end-to-end: stop the verifier op-reth, let the sequencer advance ~10 blocks, restart op-reth, and verify the verifier catches up.

## Problem

Empirical validation (with and without the op-node fix applied locally against current `develop`):

| Check | With fix | Without fix |
|---|---|---|
| Unit test `TestTryUpdateEngine_SyncingInCLModeTriggersReset` | PASS | **FAIL** — `An error is expected but got nil` |
| Unit test `TestTryUpdateEngine_SyncingInELSyncModeIsAccepted` | PASS | PASS (preserved behavior) |
| Acceptance test `TestELRestartRecovery` | PASS (~40s) | **PASS** (~41s) |

The unit tests are real regression guards. The acceptance test, as written, is not — it passes identically whether or not the fix is applied. The observed recovery path does not appear to exercise the SYNCING-response-from-cached-FCU scenario that the fix addresses. Likely explanations:

- op-reth's persistence on clean shutdown is sufficient that its canonical head survives restart, so FCU returns VALID rather than SYNCING.
- CL P2P gossip delivers newer blocks that op-reth imports via `NewPayload` before op-node's FCU with the cached heads hits the EL, so op-reth already "knows" the chain when FCU arrives.
- The 10-block gap is too small or the restart too clean to reproduce the in-memory state loss the fix assumes.

Because the acceptance test did not reliably demonstrate the bug, it has been dropped from the replayed PR (see below). The op-node fix ships with unit-test coverage only.

## What's needed

An acceptance test that **deterministically** reproduces the SYNCING-on-FCU condition after an EL event, so it FAILs on the pre-fix `engine_controller.go` and PASSes with the fix. Possible directions:

1. **Force op-reth to drop canonical state on restart** — e.g. wipe or bypass the on-disk head marker via a sysgo helper that simulates the async-persistence-lost-on-crash case.
2. **Directly drive the engine** — bypass the full restart and use a testing hook or mock EL that returns `SYNCING` to the next FCU; assert op-node emits a ResetEvent and recovers.
3. **Ungraceful restart** — if op-reth has a code path where killing the process mid-write leaves in-memory state unpersisted, reproduce that via `Kill()` rather than `Stop()`.

Option (1) or (3) is closest to the production failure mode. Option (2) is cheaper but further from reality.

## References

- PR #19384 — original fix + acceptance test (acceptance test later dropped)
- Replayed PR on current `develop`: _to be linked_
- op-node change: `op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go` — added `checkForkchoiceUpdatedStatus` gate before recording `lastForkchoice`

topPRs.title: chore(reth-optimism): fix clippy pedantic+nursery warnings
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Cleans up the ~757 warnings that `cargo clippy -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery` surfaces across the op-reth crate tree.

- `cargo clippy --fix` auto-applied the mechanical rewrites (literal separators, `#[must_use]`, `Default::default()` -> explicit types, `map_or`, `is_some_and`, etc.).
- Added a per-crate `#![allow(...)]` block at each entry point for cosmetic/architectural-cost pedantic+nursery lints (`missing_errors_doc`, `must_use_candidate`, `unreadable_literal`, `needless_pass_by_value`, `cast_*`, ...), so the remaining signal is real issues, not style noise. The allow block is adjacent to a comment explaining why each category is not worth fixing in bulk.
- Reverted the autofixer's `pub(crate) -> pub` visibility escalations that tripped the `unreachable_pub` rustc lint (test utilities, flashblocks harness, legacy `OpTransactionSigned`).
- Removed unused `tracing::{Subscriber, Callsite, Value}` imports that the autofixer inadvertently added while simplifying closures in `flashblocks/src/{cache,consensus,sequence,service}.rs`.
- Added `#[allow(unnameable_types)]` on the legacy `OpTransactionSigned` struct (exposed only through a pub trait impl).
- Added a module doc for `trie::db::models::kv`.

After this change the op-reth subset is clean under:
```
cargo clippy --no-deps -p <every-op-reth-pkg> --all-targets --tests -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings
```

Sibling packages (op-alloy, op-revm, alloy-op-*) still emit warnings — those are handled by other branches in this clippy-cleanup effort.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy --no-deps -p <op-reth pkgs> --all-targets --tests -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings` passes.
- [x] `cargo +nightly fmt -p <op-reth pkgs>` produces no diff.
- [x] `cargo build -p <op-reth pkgs>` succeeds.
- [ ] Full workspace `cargo test` (delegated to CI; local run would need sibling worker branches merged first).

topPRs.title: chore(rust): fix clippy pedantic+nursery warnings in op-alloy/op-revm/alloy-op/examples
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Clear pedantic + nursery clippy warnings across the op-alloy, op-revm, alloy-op-*, and kona-examples crates (worker D of a parallel clean-up). After this change, `cargo clippy --all-targets --tests --no-deps -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings` passes for all assigned packages.

- Mechanical fixes applied in source: unreadable literals, missing/redundant semicolons, `Default::default()` replaced with explicit types, `as` casts swapped for infallible `From`, redundant closures dropped, `match` patterns converted to `let...else`, `ok_or` -> `ok_or_else`, `u8::from(bool)` and `usize::from(bool)`, items moved before statements in tests, etc.
- API-boilerplate lints (`must_use_candidate`, `return_self_not_must_use`, `missing_errors_doc`, `missing_panics_doc`) are silenced with a crate-level `#![allow]` + short rationale so call sites stay focused on semantics.
- Targeted `#[allow]` with a justifying comment for a handful of unavoidable lints: the `fast_lz` hot-loop casts, the FastLZ stack-resident hash table, the serde `serialize_with` `&Option<T>` signature, the wildcard `use super::*` required by the `eth_precompile_fn!` macro, the `NextEvmEnvAttributes`-by-value signature consumed by op-reth, and the infallible JSON round-trip `From` impls.
- Fixed the `op-alloy-consensus` `pub(crate) fn TxDeposit::tx_type(&self)` to a true associated function and updated its single caller; similar pattern for `L1BlockInfo::tx_estimated_size_fjord`.

## Test plan
